Ahmet is an Applied Physics alumnus of TU Delft and the founder of
[JIDAI](https://jidai.nl). He maintains the project with contributions from
the open-source community.

## Why open source

Physics is best understood by building, experimenting, and verifying results
yourself. That's why the code behind every simulation, figure, and proof is
openly available for anyone to explore, reproduce, and improve.

The project is freely accessible without registration or tracking.

## How to cite

The repository has a `CITATION.cff` file in the
[Citation File Format](https://citation-file-format.github.io/). GitHub reads
it and offers "Cite this repository". It names the authors, the project
address, the repository, and the licences. It has no DOI: none exists until
the project has a release policy. A suitable citation is "Physics by
Construction", with a link to the page you used.

## How to contribute

To correct a mistake, propose a change, suggest a dataset, or propose a lesson,
open an issue from one of the forms. The [Contribute](contribute.qmd) page has
the steps.

## What this site is

Physics by Construction is a course site about physics, programming, and
proof. Lessons are ordered along one path of increasing difficulty: mechanics
with numerical simulation first, then experiments driven by AI agents, then
formal proofs in Lean.

## Who it is for

Readers who have undergraduate physics (classical mechanics, calculus, linear
algebra) and solid programming skills. Lessons state their prerequisites and
link out instead of repeating them.

## How the site is built

- Code shown in a lesson is code the build ran. Figures and numbers are the
  output of that code, regenerated on every build.
- Proofs are compiled by Lean on every change. A lesson whose code fails or
  whose proof does not compile cannot be published.
- Equations are MathML. Text, code, equations, and figures are readable with
  JavaScript turned off.
- The site is static files. It has no accounts, sets no cookies, runs no
  analytics, and loads nothing from other websites.

The [rendering check](rendering-check.qmd) page shows sample equations, code,
and a figure produced by this pipeline.
